opener.seg: [Inclosure in No. 651.—From the Levant Herald, October 21, 1895.]

div.p: The Turkish papers published yesterday morning the following official communication:

“According to the hatt of Gulhané promulgated in 1255 [Turkish calendar], in the reign of His Imperial Majesty Sultan Abdul Medjid, and to the firman of reforms published in 1272, all the subjects of His Imperial Majesty the Sultan who, without distinction of race or religion, have the necessary qualifications, are eligible for employment in the public service of the Empire; and the children of all Ottoman subjects, without distinction of race or religion, have equal facility of access to all Governmental schools. Those same laws assured the well-being and the tranquillity of all the inhabitants of the Empire.

“His Imperial Majesty Sultan Abdul Hamid, following the noble example of his illustrious predecessors, has never ceased, since his advent to the throne, to ordain measures calculated to assure the progress of the country and to increase the tranquillity and well-being of his subjects. Even now, great reforms have been introduced in the organization of the police and gendarmery; schools have been founded; railways, quays, and ports have been constructed.

“In the same manner the Imperial Government, having formed a project to make some necessary reforms in the provinces of the Empire, has decided for the present to introduce the desired reforms into some vilayets where their application would be consonant with the spirit of the Imperial hatt of Gulhané and the firman of reforms published in 1272.

“The Imperial iradé relating to these reforms has been promulgated. The reforms include the application of the organic regulation for the general administration of the vilayets of the Empire, promulgated on the 22d Chewal, 1287; the carrying out of the prescriptions of article 1 to 27 of the communal regulations ordained the 27th of March, 1292; the bestowal of the powers of justice of the peace on the councils of elders (ihtyar medjlissi); the nomination of six judicial inspectors to see to the prompt dispatch of judicial business and to inspect the prisons; the admission into the gendarmery and police of men of all the resident races, according to their respective number in each province, and in conformity with the general regulations on this matter; the nomination of a sufficient number of village guards (keui bektchissi) as provided in the code of Ottoman legislation (destour); the application of the existing regulations concerning prisons and houses of detention; the regular working of the commissions of preliminary investigation prescribed in articles 11 and 12 of the regulations for the general administration of the vilayets; strict employment of the system of escorting by a force of gendarmes and troops of the regular army the Kurdish tribes during their periodical migrations; strict application to those tribes of the law which regulates the bearing of arms; the definite settlement on the lands appointed by the Imperial Government of all the nomadic tribes; the establishment of regulations determining the attributions of the “Hamidié” regiments of cavalry, of which the men should wear uniform or arms only when they are mustered in camp for their drill; the formation of several commissions, each composed of four members, under the presidency of a cadastral director, to examine scrupulously the title deeds of all real property (emlak sendali); the annual dispatch to the provinces of four officials to inspect matters connected with real property and ascertain that no irregularities have been committed; the collection of local taxes by the moukhtars chosen by the inhabitants, and remittance of the sums thus collected to the local treasuries; the employment of public auction for the farming of the tithe, each village being put up separately. Forced labor having been already abolished, work is only claimed of the population for matters of public utility. As heretofore, it is strictly forbidden to seize the implements, seed corn, or cattle of a debtor in satisfaction of his debts, whether due to the authorities or to private individuals.”
